answer: Per-call resource token metering. Every identity must hold a unique kernel-issued session token that meters CPU and bandwidth against a prepaid budget, so each new clone requires a fresh hardware-rooted attestation costing more than a marginal agent earns. The garden of active tokens is pruned nightly: unused attestations expire unrenewed. An attacker cloning N identities pays N attestation costs plus unused-token expiry, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV, while a lone zephyr of legitimate low-volume agents stays under the metering floor.
